technical_facts: SMP support is implemented as a two-thread producer/consumer model
The rendering thread is typically the blocking factor in performance
Initial SMP attempt failed because the overhead of encoding OpenGL calls in a DLL interceptor exceeded the geometry processing gains
Current SMP implementation is integrated directly into the renderer using double buffering to allow in-place data usage
Multi-threaded programs typically have lower throughput on single CPUs compared to single-threaded programs that poll explicitly due to cache hierarchy disruption
A dual 300 MHz Intergraph Realism II system showed a 35% average speedup with SMP enabled (r_smp 1), with peaks over 90% in complex scenes
OS schedulers can introduce scheduling variances that disrupt the high-frame-rate stability required for 30+ fps applications
personality_patterns: Skeptical of 'high tech' trends for their overheads
Iterative approach to optimization (learning from previous failures)

gnosis_principles.description: Generic wrappers or interceptors (like the DLL interceptor for OpenGL) often introduce overhead that negates the performance gains of parallelism. Direct integration into the core logic is more efficient.
The performance cost of a context switch is not just CPU cycles, but the potential disruption of the cache hierarchy, which can actually decrease throughput on single-core systems.
For high-frequency real-time applications, relying on the OS scheduler to coordinate threads is often inferior to explicit polling or single-threaded execution to ensure consistent frame delivery.

heritage_patterns: Double buffering for thread-safe data access without copying
Preference for single-threaded polling over OS-managed threading for performance-critical loops

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did John Carmack's first attempt at SMP support fail?
dpo_pairs.chosen: His first attempt used a DLL that intercepted OpenGL calls to execute them on a separate processor. The overhead of encoding the commands required more bandwidth than the processing power gained from offloading the geometry, making it ineffective for most geometry types.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He didn't have enough processing power on his development system.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What are the downsides of multi-threading according to the text?
dpo_pairs.chosen: Multi-threading can lead to lower throughput on single CPUs due to cache hierarchy disruption, a loss of tight control over execution timing, and increased debugging difficulty. It also makes programs less portable.
dpo_pairs.rejected: Multi-threading is simply too slow and generally discouraged for high-performance software.
